html:
The change to the US Constitution, in force from August 1920, that bars the states and the federal government from denying citizens the vote because of their sex. It gave women across the United States the right to vote.

The campaign had begun at the Seneca Falls Convention of 1848. The amendment was first put to Congress in 1878 and was called the Anthony Amendment, after Susan B. Anthony. Some western states, starting with Wyoming in 1869, let women vote long before.

The final push came during and after World War I. Carrie Chapman Catt led the large, moderate suffrage association, while Alice Paul and her followers picketed the White House, and some were jailed and went on hunger strike. Congress passed the amendment in 1919.

Tennessee was the last state needed to ratify it, on 18 August 1920, when a young legislator, Harry Burn, changed his vote after a letter from his mother.

In practice, most Black women in the South were still kept from voting by Jim Crow laws until the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
sum: The change to the US Constitution, in force from August 1920, that bars the states and the federal government from denying citizens the vote because of their sex. It gave women across the United States the right to vote.
